rubric.why: Identifies selective permeability as the key property of the cell membrane.
rubric.description: The cell membrane is selectively permeable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the membrane’s selective permeability.

rubric.why: States that few molecules pass through while many others are blocked.
rubric.description: It allows very few molecules to pass through it while blocking many other molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both parts of the statement: few pass through and many are blocked.

modelAnswer: It is selectively-permeable. It allows very few molecules to pass through it while blocks many other molecules.

rubric.why: Identifies protein modification and packaging into vesicles as the Golgi apparatus’s key role.
rubric.description: The Golgi apparatus modifies proteins coming from rough ER and packs them into Golgi vesicles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it modifies proteins and packs them into vesicles or sacs.

rubric.why: States what happens to the Golgi vesicles after they are formed.
rubric.description: The vesicles are kept in the cell or transported to the exterior as secretions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the sacs remain in the cell or are transported outside as secretions.

modelAnswer: It modifies proteins coming from rough ER and packs them into small membrane-bound sacs called Golgi vesicles. These sacs are kept in cell or are transported to exterior in the form of secretions.

rubric.why: Describes lysosomes’ role in breaking down cellular waste or damaged organelles.
rubric.description: Lysosomes use enzymes to break cellular wastes and damaged organelles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either enzyme-mediated waste breakdown or engulfing and breaking damaged organelles.

rubric.why: Includes the additional function of storing molecules for later use.
rubric.description: Lysosomes can store certain molecules for later use.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that lysosomes store molecules for later use.

modelAnswer: Lysosomes also have enzymes for breaking cellular wastes. They also engulf the damaged organelles and break them. Lysosomes can store certain molecules for later use.

rubric.why: Identifies the folds of the mitochondrion as cristae.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the folds as cristae.

rubric.why: Explains that cristae increase the surface area available for respiration.
rubric.description: They increase the surface area for respiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking increased surface area with respiration.

modelAnswer: These folds are called cristae (singular: crista). They increase the surface area for respiration.

rubric.why: States that chromatin condenses when cell division begins.
rubric.description: When a cell starts dividing, its chromatin condenses.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing chromatin as condensing or compacting at the start of cell division.

rubric.why: States that condensed chromatin takes the form of chromosomes.
rubric.description: The condensed chromatin takes the shape of thick chromosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying chromosomes as the form taken by condensed chromatin.

modelAnswer: When a cell starts dividing, its chromatin condenses and takes the shape of thick chromosomes.

rubric.why: Identifies a stem cell as unspecialized.
rubric.description: A stem cell is an unspecialized cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a stem cell is unspecialized or undifferentiated.

rubric.why: States that it can give rise to a variety of specialized cell types.
rubric.description: It has the ability to make a variety of specialized cell types.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the ability to form or differentiate into specialized cell types.

modelAnswer: Such unspecialized cell that has the ability to make a variety of specialized cell types is called stem cell.
